product: Student loan
issue: Dealing with your lender or servicer
sub_issue: Don't agree with the fees charged
consumer_complaint_narrative:
My complaint is about Navient. 

I am a resident physician who took out money for medical school. I am now a second-year resident so this is my second year paying on the loan. I have to be on an income-based repayment plan because my income ( ~ $ XXXX ) can not possibly make the payment on my > {$200000.00} student loan. As a result of being on the income-based repayment plan, Navient forces me to re-demonstrate my income every year to re-qualify. In order to accomplish this re-demonstration ( which is a useless exercise anyway because my income barely increases annually and that number is set years ahead of time for all residency programs and it is published online ), they sent a single non-descript email on XX/XX/2018. The email does not include any indication that it might contain such a re-authorization requirement. I have attached the email with my information redacted. In order to receive the contents of the email we are required to follow the link, login, and click on a pdf link that may or may not be the most recent message ; that is easy to overlook when you get 50 emails, this one contains nothing but a link, and there is no way to tell which message on the Navient website this email is connected to. BTW, I have four post-graduate college degrees and this is not straightforward. 

Of note, Navient does not include additional reminders. They do not include an email saying anything relevant at all. In fact, all Navient emails are essentially hidden until you conduct the separate login. Then, after that single email, they emailed me in XX/XX/XXXX to say that my payment would be increasing to {$2600.00} a month. Obviously, I can not afford that while I make {$50000.00} a year. They do give me the chance to fix the problem by going back on the income-based plan. I submitted all of the information to get back to the same income-based repayment program I was previously that is currently pending. 

However, despite staying on the same payment plan and having no lapses in my payments, Navient capitalized my interest. Apparently, that is their policy. If people do not re-authorize their loan in a pre-specified window of time, Navient capitalizes their interest. In my case, that capitalization was approximately {$6000.00}. So now I am getting compounded interest around 6 % on another {$6000.00}. In other words, I get to pay an extra {$30.00} a month for the duration of my loan. All because I missed a single non-descript email. 

I am wondering what the value of such a policy for the government that I borrowed money from? That is, why would Navient be allowed to steal a huge amount of money due to missing an arbitrary re-authorization date despite staying on the exact same repayment plan. It seems like a scam. We are basically borrowing money from our own government and Navient is being allowed to skim money off the top.

sub_product: General-purpose credit card or charge card
sub_issue: Charged too much interest
consumer_complaint_narrative:
NAVY FEDERAL CREDIT UNION IS IN VIOLATION OF THE SOLDIERS AND SAILERS ACT. THEY ARE NOT SUPPOSE TO CHARGE INTEREST ON AN ACCOUNT Benefit and Protection No. 1 The six percent interest rate cap. 50 U.S.C. 3937 The SCRA limits the amount of interest that may be charged on certain financial obligations that were incurred prior to military service to no more than six percent per year, including most fees. 50 U.S.C. 3937 ( a ) ( 1 ) & ( d ) ( 1 ). In order to have the interest rate on a financial obligation such as a credit card or a mortgage capped at six percent per year, a servicemember must provide the creditor with written notice and a copy of his or her military orders or other appropriate indicator of military service ( such as a letter from a commanding officer ). Id. at 3937 ( b ) ( 1 ). The written notice and proof of military service must be provided to the creditor within 180 days of the end of the servicemembers military service. Id. 

In response, a creditor must forgive not defer interest greater than six percent per year. See 50 U.S.C. 3937 ( a ) ( 2 ). The creditor must forgive this interest retroactively. See id. at 3937 ( a ) ( 1 ) & ( b ) ( 2 ). The creditor is also prohibited from accelerating the payment of principal in response to a properly made request for a six percent interest rate cap. Id. at 3937 ( a ) ( 3 ).

For mortgages, interest is capped at six percent during the entire period of military service and for one year after the period of military service. 50 U.S.C. 3937 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ). For all other obligations, interest is capped at six percent only for the duration of the period of military service. Id. at 3937 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ).

A hypothetical under Section 3937 of the SCRA, 50 U.S.C. 3937 :
John Doe takes out a mortgage and then enters military service. Captain John Doe is in military service continuously for 20 years. Captain Doe retires from military service and on the 179th day of his retirement asks that the interest rate on his mortgage be lowered to six percent per year. Captain Doe provides his creditor with a written notice and a copy of all of his military orders. The creditor must forgive the entire 20 years of interest that was at a rate greater than six percent inclusive of fees and an additional year of interest going forward. See, generally, 50 U.S.C. 3937.

The following types of financial obligations, among others, are currently eligible for the six percent SCRA interest rate benefit : credit cards ; automobile, ATV, boat and other vehicle loans ; mortgages ; home equity loans ; and student loans. See, e.g., 50 U.S.C. 3937 ( d ) ( 2 ).

On August 14, 2008, President Bush signed into law the Higher Education Opportunity Act, P.L. 110-315, that, among other things, amended 20 U.S.C. 1078 ( d ) to make federally guaranteed student loans protected under the SCRA. That means that prior to August 14, 2008, the SCRA did not cover federally guaranteed student loans. So, for federally guaranteed student loans that originated before August 14, 2008, such as student loans that originated under the Federal Family Education Loan ( FFEL ) Program and Direct Loans from the Department of Education, the servicemember borrower is not covered by the SCRA.

A student loan hypothetical under Section 3937 of the SCRA, 50 U.S.C. 3937 : John Doe takes out five private student loans prior to entering into military service. After entering military service, Servicemember Doe consolidates his five loans into one loan. Six months later, he hears about the SCRAs six percent interest rate cap and requests that the interest rate on his loan be lowered to six percent per year. He sends in a written notice and a copy of his military orders.

Question : Is Servicemember Doe entitled to the six percent interest rate cap?

Answer : Only for the period of time between when he entered military service and when he consolidated his private student loans. Servicemember Does existing student loan originated during a period of military service. See 50 U.S.C. 3937 ( a ) ( 1 ).

sub_product: General-purpose credit card or charge card
issue: Advertising and marketing, including promotional offers
sub_issue: Didn't receive advertised or promotional terms
consumer_complaint_narrative:
Dear American Express, This complaint is relative to a public welcome offer listed on the American Express Surpass XXXX offer that advertises a free weekend night after the first anniversary of card membership. The offer also includes a XXXX XXXX XXXX bonus points after spending {$3000.00} in purchases within the first 3 months of card membership. While the spending requirement has been met and the XXXX XXXX XXXX bonus points received, I have yet to receive my weekend night certificate upon my annual membership date ( XX/XX/XXXX ) or payment of my annual fee, even within the generous 6 - 8 week window listed in the terms and conditions of the offer. 

I have contacted American Express through the websites chat and was unable to find resolution to this issue. I first contacted XXXX who then forwarded me to XXXX. Our main point of contention can be summarized as the following : There was a free night certificate for the XXXX  surpass card but on the XX/XX/XXXX, we changed the terms of card as we changed the name from XXXX Surpass to XXXX Ascend. A condition was added that the Card member needs to spend {$15000.00} in a calendar year to earn that free night certificate. Hence, the Card member 's whose anniversary date was after XX/XX/XXXX will only get the free night once the spending is met on the account. 

I disagree and here are the reasons why this argument does not hold : 1. I mentioned that if I were to apply for an AMEX card with a signup bonus today and tomorrow AMEX immediately pulls the offer, changes the card slightly, and removes the welcome language from any offer terms and conditions, would I be grandfathered into the new  terms and no longer be eligible for the bonus? In response, XXXX states that The card is eligible for the welcome bonus which it is linked with and I agree. The weekend annual night certificate was included as a special welcome bonus and NOT as a traditional feature of the Surpass card. Yet, she contradicts herself by saying, A condition was added that the Card member needs to spend {$15000.00} in a calendar year to earn that free night certificate. Hence, the Card member 's whose anniversary date was after XX/XX/XXXX will only get the free night once the spending is met on the account. 
2. She argues that the Ascends universal feature of awarding an annual weekend night certificate after {$15000.00} of calendar year spend is a valid substitute of the one-time annual weekend certificate from Surpass limited welcome bonus offer. She makes no distinction between the Ascend or Surpass weekend night certificates regardless of why or how they are awarded. On the other hand, opening a Surpass with a welcome offer but completing the requirements shortly after the change to Ascend still satisfies the opening bonus, but XXXX insists each certificate is now mutually exclusive to each card. Still, there are counterexamples from XXXX users who could secure both during the start of the Ascend. If Shannons logic were to hold and instead the Ascend card offered no annual certificate for {$15000.00} calendar year spend or at the very least some incentive other than an annual night certificate ( {$100.00} statement credit, XXXX points, etc. ), then the Surpass annual free night certificate would have clearly been awarded on account anniversary. She makes no distinctions between annual night certificates, despite one being a unique welcome offer and the other a general feature of the card. 
3. XXXX mentions, American Express reserves the right to modify or revoke offer at any time. I am sure there are certain boundaries in which AMEX can enforce this without any form of repercussions, though in this case it would be certainly a disingenuous and silly mechanism to avoid upholding its end of the bargain for what should have been an extremely simple case and resolution. The account has been in good standing, does not involve fraudulent activity, and only needed to be open for one year. In return, all AMEX needed to do was award just a single ( 1 ) weekend night certificate. I fail to see how refreshing a card or changing its name somehow justifies invalidating the weekend certificate bonus requirement that an account be open for one ( 1 ) year.

'' So it was confirmed that I have not gotten a statement indicating a problem with payments. We also confirmed that the secondary phone number on my account was a phone number we haven't used in over 2 years! So after not sending me written statements or correspondence, XXXX sent a longstanding customer with no history of failing to make payments to collections. 

I was then transferred to Pinnacle who could find no record of me in their system. The lady I spoke to told me to call XXXX back because she thought it was a mistake. I called XXXX back and was told that I had just been transferred to collections that day. I told the man that I just wanted to know what the problem with my account was and make any necessary payment. He said I would have to talk to Pinnacle and he couldn't help me and he transferred me back to Pinnacle. The man I talked to me at Pinnacle this time told me that actually hadn't completed transferring my file yet and he wouldn't be able to tell me what was going on until the file had finished transferring. I am still shocked that even though my file hadn't actually transferred to collections and I was reaching out to XXXX to resolve whatever issue there was they were refusing to not only tell me what the problem was, but to let me fix it at that point. 

Later that night, the man from Pinnacle called me back and I was shocked to be told that I owe over {$1400.00}! Part of that amount was {$300.00} in " debt collection fees '' that Pinnacle charges. After being told that I have to pay off this shocking debt before the end of the year or I would be charged another debt collection fee, I agreed to make a payment. I was honestly so  shocked by all of this, I wasn't processing information properly. I still do not understand what is wrong with my account, I was forced to make a payment to a shady debt collector, and all of this based on incredibly poor communication about the status of my account by XXXX. Later that evening US Bank called again while I was on the phone with my wife discussing my family tragedy. Unfortunately I ran out of time to get back to them and didn't bring it back up until this month. I reached out about this issue and long-term payment relief options ( related to COVID-19 ). In Federal Trade Commission v. XXXX ( XX/XX/2009 ) the federal district court decided in favor of the Federal Trade Commission that a collection agency must operate within strict guidelines in the collection of a debt. The criteria are as follows : 1 ) The debt must still be enforceable within the state of procurement or where the original obligator resides, or a combination of both. 
2 ) The debt collector must be licensed and bonded if applicable within the state in which it is trying to collect, if the debt is collectable. 
3 ) The validation of debt ownership must be proved, without exception. 
There is no statement on the attached collection that the debt is no longer enforceable. The collection agency stipulates that XXXX obtained a judgment against me. There can not be a lawsuit as the legal time limit to enforce a summary judgment action has passed. 
Even though the collection letter states that illegal, abusive, deceptive and unfair debt collections are illegal, this collection in its entirety is just that, a deceptive illegal attempt to collect a debt that is no longer enforceable. 
I demand that all my information be purged immediately by Midwest Recovery Systems and XXXX, and that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) take the necessary steps to sanction both companies for using such abusive collection tactics.

Knowing I was out of the country ( XXXX ) they made no mention that my due date for my current balance of {$2400.00} was in around eight or nine days and if I was late, an interest charge of 29.99 % would be applied to this new large charge of {$33000.00} even though it was not late.

Then, to add insult to injury, they charged that interest rate of roughly 29.99 % on the {$33000.00} hotel charge made onXX/XX/XXXX which was not late it was not even due yet ( they charged {$460.00} interest ).

Detailed Summary : On XXXX XXXX, 2022, at approximately XXXX XXXX, I received a telephone call from a registered USAA number while driving on the XXXX highway from XXXX to XXXX in Arizona. The speaker informed me that USAA had flagged charges on my account. The speaker proceeded to list out a series of charges and stated that an unknown person had accessed and withdrawn money from an in-person branch of USAA in XXXX XXXX XXXX Texas. 
The speaker then asked me to read out a code that was sent to my phone via text. I briefly checked my text messages to provide the requested code and checked my app to see if there were any discrepancies. Shortly after that, I asked if the speaker could call me back after I got home to ensure the subject matter at issue had my full focus and attention. 
Once I arrived home, I checked the USAA app again and waited for USAA to call me back. After waiting for USAA to call me back and having not received a call, I called USAA at approximately XXXX pm. I reported the information that had been provided to me. Specifically, I explained that USAA had contacted me to report fraudulent charges on my account, including ( 1 ) a deposit from a bad check for {$16000.00} into my checking account, ( 2 ) a {$2500.00} cash advance from my credit card deposited into my savings account, ( XXXX ) a {$390.00} dollar cashier 's check from my savings account going to an unrecognized address, and ( XXXX ) a {$2500.00} cashier 's check from my savings account going to an unrecognized address. 
Upon reporting this activity, I learned that a fraudulent individual had contacted me, not USAA. USAA filed the information that I reported as general fraud and began to investigate what happened. Next, I contacted USAA account takeover and was temporarily locked out of my account while USAA conducted its investigation. After contacting USAA account takeover, I contacted the checking and savings department and requested they cancel the checks that were sent. That department informed me that, " We are unable to cancel cashier 's checks after they have been sent, the fraud and security department should refund the lost funds. I also contacted the credit department and informed them that I did not deposit that large amount into my credit account and did not authorize a cash advance. 
Over the weeks that followed, USAAs analysis of what transpired on XXXX XXXX, 2022 vacillated between finding no evidence of fraud to claiming that I sabotaged my own bank account to determining that I fell victim to a phishing attack. 
I continued to follow up with USAA about the status of the Companys investigation and consistently affirmed that I was the victim of a phishing scam. USAA documented the cash advance on my credit card as fraud and the cash advance was refunded, but I have never been reimbursed for my lost savings.

We have a fixed rate auto loan with XXXX XXXX. We pay extra on the loan most months and noticed that the amount due on the bill fluctuates each month which should not be possible given that the loan terms are fixed. ( Background : My career and XXXX XXXX are both in finance ). 

I called XXXX XXXX today and spoke to employee ID # XXXX. I described the problem and was forced to listen to a recording about how additional funds were not applied to principle unless one were to jump through a bunch of hoops after each payment to get the additional funds applied to principle. What they do instead is apply the additional payment to future payments. 

By doing this they are overcharging me in interest as the additional payments are not impacting the outstanding principal balance they are intended for. The outstanding principal balance is the input in the calculation made each month when payment is made to derive how much of the payment goes to interest with the remainder going to principle ( as per any standard amortization schedule ). 

This practice is dishonest if not illegal. Why would anyone decide to give the lender money in advance if it has no impact on the total interest paid over the life of the loan? Literally they are taking this money as if I were now lending them cash interest free or if I am being paid interested on my advanced payments, they are creating a potential tax liability for me that isnt getting accounted for when I pay income tax. 

I asked the kid on the other line to tell me where on the loan documents I could find this unconventional and possibly illegal practice defined. He could only point me to the bill and didn't seem to realize that the bill was not an addendum to the contract or even on the same legal level. Finally, he asked " How can I help you? '' as if it wasn't clear what I was requesting to happen. The call was ended unresolved. 

Later after reading the loan documents I found where credits were applied in reverse order and it suggests that interest is also paid ( see attached documentation ).

Correction of billing errors ( b ) Billing error ( 4 ) The creditor 's failure to reflect properly on a statement, a payment made by the obligor or a credit issued to the obligor. product: Credit reporting, credit repair services, or other personal consumer reports
sub_issue: Old information reappears or never goes away
consumer_complaint_narrative:
THIS COMPLAINT IS IN REGARD TO A CREDIT INQUIRY EXISTING ON MY XXXX CREDIT REPORT PASSED THE LEGAL REPORTING STATUTE OF TWO YEARS. THIS COMPLAINT IS AGAINST THE CREDITOR TD BANK XXXX XXXX THAT IS FURNISHING THIS OUTDATED INFORMATION TO XXXX. THIS COMPLAINT IS NOT AGAINST XXXX  AT THIS TIME. 
This is a complaint arising under Sections 5 ( a ), 5 ( m ), 13 ( b ), and 16 ( a ) of the Federal Trade Commission Act ( FTC Act ), 15 U.S.C. 45 ( a ), 45 ( m ) ( 1 ) ( A ), 53 ( b ), and 56 ( a ) ; the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681-1681x ; and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p, to  obtain monetary civil penalties, a permanent injunction, restitution, disgorgement, and other equitable relief for the Defendants violations of the FCRA, the FDCPA, and Section 5 of the FTC Act. 
XXXX  provides consumer personal credit reports to regional and national credit grantors, attempting to issue both commercial and consumer credit. XXXX  regularly furnishes consumer credit reports to Creditors electronically. XXXX  is an entity who regularly and in the ordinary course of business furnishes information to XXXX  or more Creditors about its transactions or experiences with its consumers. 
XXXX  routinely receives complaints from consumers who claim they do not owe the debt or that an account is invalid or incorrect. In numerous instances, I have notified XXXX  at the address specified for such disputes that XXXX  is reporting inaccurate information concerning my consumer credit. As a victim of identity theft and the XXXX Data Breach I expect the information in my consumer report to be accurate and my disputes taken seriously. 
XXXX  has continued to report inaccurate information to the Creditors even after receiving such notice and accompanying proof. In numerous instances, I have disputed the information appearing on my consumer credit report in writing to XXXX. XXXX  receives most notices of disputes from a consumer in electronic format, through automated consumer dispute verification ( ACDV ) forms provided on XXXX  website. 
Pursuant to Section 623 ( b ) ( 1 ) of the FCRA, XXXX, as a furnisher of information to the Creditors, is required to conduct an investigation of the disputed information upon receipt of a notice of dispute from a Consumer. For certain types of disputes, such as those where the consumer claims the account is not his or hers or belongs to someone with a similar name, it is XXXX  s policy and practice only to compare the name, social security number, date of birth, and address in XXXX  s computer database with the information provided on ACDV forms. Where three of the four items match, XXXX  will report to the Consumer that it has verified the information it furnished as accurate. It is XXXX s policy that only after the consumer has alleged the same type of account inaccuracy more than four times will the matter become assigned to a supervisor to do further investigation. Because XXXX  collects accounts that are often old, information in its computer files may not be accurate for a variety of reasons, including incorrect updating of addresses, errors in recording names and information, and problems with the original Creditors records. 
In disputes involving identity theft or fraud allegations, XXXX  s policies provide that if the existing account codes and notes in its records do not contain any reference to a prior claim of fraud, XXXX  will verify the previously reported information without conducting any investigation prior to such verification. In numerous instances, despite written or oral notification from consumers disputing the accuracy or completeness of alleged debts, XXXX   continued to furnish the information to the Creditors without communicating that the information was disputed by the consumer. Section 623 ( a ) of the FCRA describes the duties of furnishers to provide accurate information to Creditors. Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ) prohibits furnishers from providing information relating to a consumer to any Creditor if i. the person has been notified by the consumer, at the address specified by the person for such notices, that specific information is inaccurate ; and ii. the information is, in fact, inaccurate. In numerous instances, I have contacted XXXX  at the address specified by XXXX  to dispute information furnished by XXXX  to a Creditor and to notify XXXX  that the information is inaccurate. 
In numerous instances, I have also provided information such as the consumers drivers license, social security number, and/or proof of residence to confirm my identity. The acts and practices alleged above constitute violations of Section 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ) of the FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ). Pursuant to Section 621 ( a ) ( 1 ) of the FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681s ( a ) ( 1 ), the acts and practices alleged above also constitute unfair or deceptive acts or practices in violation of Section 5 ( a ) of the FTC Act, 15 U.S.C. 45 ( a ). 
TD BANK XXXX XXXX is also a furnisher of inaccurate credit information and is just as liable as XXXX. A recorded statement from XXXX  states that TD BANK XXXX XXXX is the one responsible for removing this information from my credit report. As it currently stands XXXX  nor TD BANK XXXX XXXX has not validated or verified the accuracy of this inquiry. They also failed to remove the inquiry from my credit report after the two year statute of limitation. The following outdated inquiries are being furnished by TD BANK XXXX XXXX and are being reported by XXXX. 
Inquiry Entry Date Legal Removal Date Inquiry listed as XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/XXXX As of XX/XX/XXXX these inquires are still being reported.

I am very confident that you are in violation of the ( FCRA ) and ( FCBA ) sections ( 1666, 1666a. 1666b., and 1666c. ) as stated below : 1666. Correction of billing errors ( b ) Billing error ( 4 ) The creditor 's failure to reflect properly on a statement, a payment made by the obligor or a credit issued to the obligor. ( XXXX ) A computation error or similar error of an accounting nature of the creditor on a statement. ( 6 ) Failure to transmit the statement required under section 1637 ( b ) of this title to the last address of the obligor which has been disclosed to the creditor, unless that address was furnished less than twenty days before the end of the billing cycle for which the statement is required. ( 7 ) Any other error described in regulations of the Bureau. 1666a. Regulation of credit reports ( a ) Reports by creditor on obligor 's failure to pay amount regarded as billing error After receiving a notice from an obligor as provided in section 1666 ( a ) of this title, a creditor or his agent may not directly or indirectly threaten to report to any person adversely on the obligor 's credit rating or credit standing because of the obligor 's failure to pay the amount indicated by the obligor under section 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title, and such amount may not be reported as delinquent to any third party until the creditor has met the requirements of section 1666 of this title and has allowed the obligor the same number of days ( not less than ten ) thereafter to make payment as is provided under the credit agreement with the obligor for the payment of undisputed amounts. ( b ) Reports by creditor on delinquent amounts in dispute ; notification of obligor of parties notified of delinquency If a creditor receives a further written notice from an obligor that an amount is still in dispute within the time allowed for payment under subsection ( a ) of this section, a creditor may not report to any third party that the amount of the obligor is delinquent because the obligor has failed to pay an amount which he has indicated under section 1666 ( a ) ( 2 ) of this title, unless the creditor also reports that the amount is in dispute and, at the same time, notifies the obligor of the name and address of each party to whom the creditor is reporting information concerning the delinquency. ( c ) Reports by creditor of subsequent resolution of delinquent amounts A creditor shall report any subsequent resolution of any delinquencies reported pursuant to subsection ( b ) to the parties to whom such delinquencies were initially reported. 1666b. Timing of payments ( a ) Time to make payments A creditor may not treat a payment on a credit card account under an open end consumer credit plan as late for any purpose, unless the creditor has adopted reasonable procedures designed to ensure that each periodic statement including the information required by section 1637 ( b ) of this title is mailed or delivered to the consumer not later than 21 days before the payment due date. I DEMAND to see proof that I was mailed my statement to the correct address notifying me of both payment due date and delinquency of payment on the account. If you can not provide 100 % Verifiable proof and proper documentation that the CREDITOR fulfilled its obligations under the ( FCBA ) and ( FCRA ), I therefore demand these late payments be removed from my account or I will be forced to be in contact with the Attorney General of my State and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. consumer_complaint_narrative:
On XX/XX/2021, I initiated a transfer of {$100.00} from my checking account to my money market account. I received an error on the transfer and tried a few more times, unable to get it to go through. On the morning of XX/XX/2021, I contacted Schwab customer service because I continued to get an error message. A team member on the brokerage side attempted to do the transfer for me but also encountered an error. She transferred me to a representative on the banking side who was able to get the transfer through. 

That afternoon, I looked at my account and saw that nine transfers of {$100.00} left my checking account. It appeared that one went through for every time I or a customer service rep attempted to make the transfer. However, when I looked at the brokerage account, only one transfer of {$100.00} went through. This left {$800.00} missing from my checking account. 

Since XX/XX/XXXX I have spoken with multiple representatives at Schwab. Given their long hold times, I have spent many hours on the phone waiting for help. Each customer service rep I have spoken with has told me the issue was known and was being worked on. Each promised me the issue would be fixed by the following business day. As of today, XX/XX/XXXX, the issue still hasnt been fixed. 

If I would have overdrawn my account I would have incurred bank fees as a penalty. Instead, in this situation, I have to float {$800.00}, money that can not be spent or invested, because of a banking error that Schwab staff is seemingly unable to resolve. I have been told by some reps that the eight erroneous transactions would be voided and the funds returned to my checking. Others have told me the eight erroneous transfers would be completed and the {$800.00} moved to my brokerage. I am unable to understand why this issue can not easily be resolved and have completely lost both patience with this process and faith that my money is safe with Schwab. 

It is worth noting that in the middle of this issue, I encountered another issue with Schwab whereby a stop limit set on a security I once held with Schwab but later transferred to XXXX was activated. I had an alert in my account showing I owed those securities back. Thankfully, they were able to void that transaction but it only adds to my impression of Schwab having issues with the way in which their systems hold and manage my money.

This complaint supersedes the complaint which I filed against these parties. The complaint involves XXXX parties, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) and its collection agency, Collection Bureau of America ( Bureau ). 

Essentially, the Bureau submitted a bill to me containing false statements as to what I had been paid and what I owed due to charges my insurance company disallowed. When I demanded a bill reflecting any adjustments by my insurer, the Bureau refused to provide it and threatened to report me to the credit reporting agencies, as it knew that reporting accurate information would have revealed its fraud. Because these practices appear widespread, an investigation is necessary and enforcement action may be as well. 

The complaint relates to my hospital stay in XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX and XXXX XXXX. I was treated both in the emergency room and the main hospital. 

I received a bill from XXXX in early XXXX claiming {$5500.00} for services rendered while hospitalized. This bill was the only one I received for a stay in which the total billed amount was in excess of {$120000.00}. I contacted the billing departments for both the emergency room and regular hospital physicians. Both reported that all services had been paid in full. 

I contacted my insurer, advised them of these facts, and asked them to investigate. XXXX reported that it could find no record of a bill rendered by XXXX. 

In the fall of XXXX, I was contacted by an XXXX at the Bureau. She initially claimed that the insurer had not paid the {$5500.00} and that I owed it. In a second call she claimed that I had been paid approximately {$5200.00} and that I owed that. I explained that I wanted a statement of itemized charges together with the insurer 's adjustments. She refused to provide one. 

Thereafter, my insurer and XXXX communicated and discovered the reason for the lack of progress in my investigation. XXXX had reported the charges under a different physician, XXXX XXXX, than the physician reported to me, XXXX XXXX. Hence, when I was asking for information from XXXX, they were not searching under the right name. Based on the records available to XXXX, they advised that {$1100.00} of XXXX claim had been disallowed, and that this fact had been communicated to XXXX. 

Hence the following statements, made through the United States mails and by interstate wire communictions, were false and known to be false by XXXX and the Bureau when made. 

1. That I had been paid {$5500.00}. 
2. That I owed {$5500.00}. 
3. That I owed interest on the {$5500.00}. 

In addition, XXXX and the Bureau 's failure to provide a bill indicating the insurer 's adjustments were made in an effort to conceal conduct that they knew to be unlawful. 

I do not have the ability to scan documents on this computer but I can provide copies if contacted at the cotaqct information below. 

My advice to consumers is twofold. Never accept as true a medical bill that does not reflect the adjustments made by the insurer. With more than 15 separate entries on the bill, the chances of this happening after action by the insurer are virtually nil.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
I am a new Bank of America credit card customer. I set up Auto-Pay immediately when I receive my new account information. The settings were to pay my entire statement amount on the due date. Unfortunately, this feature offered by BoFA fails to do what it advertises. Using Auto-Pay for my first two statement cycles has racked up over {$100.00} in non-refundable interest, along with overcharging my checking account by {$4000.00}. Reporting these bank errors to the company has not made any difference in their Auto-Pay product, nor a monetary refund for their mistakes. 

Bank of America 's Auto-Pay feature made the following errors : 1. After setting up Auto-Pay to pay for the full statement balance on the due date, it does not immediately go into effect, unlike all other credit cards, utility companies, and other billing services I have used. The website did not inform me of this delay, and only a customer service agent told me. Therefore, my first statement payment was late as I had to manually pay the statement. I was charged interest and a late fee, though I had already set up Auto-Pay. 
2. Auto-Pay then deducted the 1st + 2nd statement balances from my account, leaving me with a negative - {$4000.00} balance. 
3. The Auto-Pay payment that went through did not clear on the due date of the 2nd statement. I was again charged interest for being late, even though Auto-Pay had OVERdeducted from my checking account. 

Bank of America has refunded my late fee but has refused to refund my interest fees. Bank of America has over deducted from my checking account by - {$4000.00}, a salt in the wound as I'm losing interest on this overcharge. 

In conclusion, Bank of America is advertising a convenient fool-proof solution ( Auto-Pay ) that does not pay the correct amount on time and charges the customer interest for its product failings. Auto-Pay 's failings need to be correctly advertised, and Bank of America is using this feature to falsely charge their most responsible customers, the customers who even sign up for Auto-Pay, fees and interest for simply trusting its products.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
This is to describe the nature of the dispute regarding the American Express Everyday Card applied for XX/XX/2019. I will outline the ways in which American Express is currently violating the FTCs Section 5 UDAP. 

To keep it brief, I applied for a card and they approved me for an XXXX balance. This is card is a balance transfer card. The AMEX Everyday card touted 15 months of 0 % intro APR for purchases and balance transfers and {$0.00} transfer fees and {$0.00} annual fees. 

Once I received the card I called to ask about increasing my limit so I could transfer a larger amount to this card and that would help me reduce my overall balances since I wouldnt be paying interest based on the terms provided. This is where I began to learn of the limits that were not disclosed and are not available to public knowledge. I was told by a representative that the policy from AMEX is the limit allowed to transfer no matter the available limit of credit on ANY card member is the lesser of {$5000.00} or 75 % of the credit limit minus fees. This policy has been in effect since XX/XX/2019. Also I was told that there is only one transfer available per card. I would like to include that I had 3 conversations with 3 different individuals about this matter and got 3 different answers, but this one was the most concise when the  question was asked, what is AMEXs balance transfer policy? 

I had read almost every line on all of the documents I had received to see what the limits were, what percent of credit limit, what amount and nothing was listed. The only language I could find was as follows on the balance transfer application from a solicitation for the credit card : 1. You may request a balance transfer up to the eligible transfer amount, which will be based on your credit worthiness and other factors including your account history with American Express. 
2. The fee for balance transfers is {$0.00}. Balance transfers must be requested within 60 days from account opening.

3. Balances may not be transferred from any account issued by American Express or affiliates.

4. Please refer to terms and conditions insert for complete detailsshown in ( Doc B ). 
In the event that you request multiple transfers, each transfer will be processed in the order that we deem appropriate for business or other reasons up to the applicable limit.

I will expand on 2 of these items.

Item 1 : This states a member can request a transfer UP TO THE ELIGIBLE TRANSFER AMOUNT. This amount is defined by American Express internal policies only when speaking to a representative as the lesser of {$5000.00} or 75 % of the credit limit minus fees, yet not disclosed here. It is also not in any marketing documents. It then follows to say it is based on credit worthiness and other factors, etc. Those may be true, but not the full extent of the determination to what the actual balance transfer amount is. This is a misrepresentation of the statement of fact.

Item 4 is not as important, but it also seems that you can not actually make more than 1 balance transfer even if you request 5. So the statement that processing and deeming appropriate is all just filler and misdirection because the applicable limit is 1. Again, more omissions and misrepresentations regarding American Expresses balance transfer policies. 

In the terms and conditions for complete details about balance transfers there is more ambiguous language. It states the minimum limit of transfer that can be requested, but again no mention of the actual maximum limits. Then the determination of : The eligible balance transfer amount will be : I ) less than your credit limit ; II ) determined based on your credit worthiness and other factors including your account history with American Express ; and III ) Provided to you after your application has been approved. 

I would argue that this is an effort by American Express to omit information that American Express knows would affect the applications and approvals and usage of cards if provided. Therefore a lot of fluff regarding qualifications is being used to try and get around the main policy for all members and is being purposefully left out as it could lead to fewer applications and approvals when compared to other cards who do disclose such information in their marketing materials. 

After all of this information showing American Express was aware of a policy regarding balance transfer limits. This is a complaint arising under Sections 5 ( a ), 5 ( m ), 13 ( b ), and 16 ( a ) of the Federal Trade Commission Act ( FTC Act ), 15 U.S.C. 45 ( a ), 45 ( m ) ( 1 ) ( A ), 53 ( b ), and 56 ( a ) ; the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA, 15 U.S.C. 1681-1681x ; and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p, to obtain monetary civil penalties, a permanent injunction, restitution, disgorgement, and other equitable relief for the Defendants violations of the FCRA, the FDCPA, and Section 5 of the FTC Act.

XXXX provides consumer personal credit reports to regional and national credit grantors, attempting to issue both commercial and consumer credit. XXXX regularly furnishes consumer credit reports to Creditors electronically. XXXX is an entity who regularly and in the ordinary course of business furnishes information to one or more Creditors about its transactions or experiences with its consumers. XXXX routinely receives complaints from consumers who claim they do not owe the debt.

In numerous instances, I have notified XXXX at the address specified for such disputes that XXXX  is reporting inaccurate information concerning my consumer credit. As a victim of identity theft and the XXXX Data Breach I expect the information in my consumer report to be accurate and my disputes taken seriously. XXXX  has continued to report inaccurate information to the Creditors even after receiving such notice and accompanying proof. In numerous instances, I have disputed the information appearing on my consumer credit report in writing to XXXX   reporting the information. XXXX receives most notices of disputes from a consumer in electronic format, through automated consumer dispute verification ( ACDV ) forms provided on DEFENDANTS website.

Pursuant to Section 623 ( b ) ( 1 ) of the FCRA, XXXX, as a furnisher of information to the Creditors, is required to conduct an investigation of the disputed information upon receipt of a notice of dispute from a Consumer. For certain types of disputes, such as those where the consumer claims the account is not his or hers or belongs to someone with a similar name, it is XXXX s policy and practice only to compare the name, social security number, date of birth, and address in XXXX s computer database with the information provided on ACDV forms. Where three of the four items match, XXXX  will report to the Consumer that it has verified the information it furnished as accurate. It is XXXX  s policy that only after the consumer has alleged the same type of account inaccuracy more than four times will the matter become assigned to a supervisor to do further investigation. Because XXXX collects accounts that are often old, information in its computer files may not be accurate for a variety of reasons, including incorrect updating of addresses, errors in recording names and information, and problems with the original Creditors records.

In disputes involving identity theft or fraud allegations, XXXX s policies provide that if the existing account codes and notes in its records do not contain any reference to a prior claim of fraud, XXXX will verify the previously reported information without conducting any investigation prior to such verification.

In numerous instances, despite written or oral notification from consumers disputing the accuracy or completeness of alleged debts, Defendant XXXX continued to furnish the information to the Creditors without communicating that the information was disputed by the consumer.

( a ) Block. Except as otherwise provided in this section, a consumer reporting agency shall block the reporting of any information in the file of a consumer that the consumer identifies as information that resulted from an alleged identity theft, not later than 4 business days after the date of receipt by such agency of ( 1 ) appropriate proof of the identity of the consumer ; ( 2 ) a copy of an identity theft report ; ( 3 ) the identification of such information by the consumer ; and ( 4 ) a statement by the consumer that the information is not information relating to any transaction by the consumer. ( b ) Notification. A consumer reporting agency shall promptly notify the furnisher of information identified by the consumer under subsection ( a ) of this section ( 1 ) that the information may be a result of identity theft ; ( 2 ) that an identity theft report has been filed ; ( 3 ) that a block has been requested under this section ; and ( 4 ) of the effective dates of the block. ( c ) Authority to decline or rescind. ( 1 ) In general. A consumer reporting agency may decline to block, or may rescind any block, of information relating to a consumer under this section, if the consumer reporting agency reasonably determines that ( A ) the information was blocked in error or a block was requested by the consumer in error ; ( B ) the information was blocked, or a block was requested by the consumer, on the basis of a material misrepresentation of fact by the consumer relevant to the request to block ; or ( C ) the consumer obtained possession of goods, services, or money as a result of the blocked transaction or transactions. ( 2 ) Notification to consumer. If a block of information is declined or rescinded under this subsection, the affected consumer shall be notified promptly, in the same manner as consumers are notified of the reinsertion of information under section 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ) of this title. ( 3 ) Significance of block. For purposes of this subsection, if a consumer reporting agency rescinds a block, the presence of information in the file of a consumer prior to the blocking of such information is not evidence of whether the consumer knew or should have known that the consumer obtained possession of any goods, services, or money as a result of the block. ( d ) Exception for resellers. ( 1 ) No reseller file. This section shall not apply to a consumer reporting agency, if the consumer reporting agency ( A ) is a reseller ; ( B ) is not, at the time of the request of the consumer under subsection ( a ) of this section, otherwise furnishing or reselling a consumer report concerning the information identified by the consumer ; and ( C ) informs the consumer, by any means, that the consumer may report the identity theft to the Bureau to obtain consumer information regarding identity theft. ( 2 ) Reseller with file. The sole obligation of the consumer reporting agency under this section, with regard to any request of a consumer under this section, shall be to block the consumer report maintained by the consumer reporting agency from any subsequent use, if ( A ) the consumer, in accordance with the provisions of subsection ( a ) of this section, identifies, to a consumer reporting agency, information in the file of the consumer that resulted from identity theft ; and ( B ) the consumer reporting agency is a reseller of the identified information. ( 3 ) Notice. In carrying out its obligation under paragraph ( 2 ), the reseller shall promptly provide a notice to the consumer of the decision to block the file. Such notice shall contain the name, address, and telephone number of each consumer reporting agency from which the consumer information was obtained for resale. ( e ) Exception for verification companies. The provisions of this section do not apply to a check services company, acting as such, which issues authorizations for the purpose of approving or processing negotiable instruments, electronic fund transfers, or similar methods of payments, except that, beginning 4 business days after receipt of information described in paragraphs ( 1 ) through ( 3 ) of subsection ( a ) of this section, a check services company shall not report to a national consumer reporting agency described in section 1681a ( p ) of this title, any information identified in the subject identity theft report as resulting from identity theft. ( f ) Access to blocked information by law enforcement agencies. No provision of this section shall be construed as requiring a consumer reporting agency to prevent a Federal, State, or local law enforcement agency from accessing blocked information in a consumer file to which the agency could otherwise obtain access under this subchapter.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
Rather than investigating results internally, Early Warning Services improperly uses consumer information by sending any disputes consumers have directly to financial institutions that don't have any authorization to remove fraudulent, harmful and inaccurate info, as reported by Early Warnings Services. I have compiled notes on phone calls with Early Warning Services where employees admitted that my data produced by Early Warning Services shouldn't have sent to all banks listed on the report. EWS should have corrected the comprehensive consumer report and remove the inaccurate information displayed. For example, XXXX XXXX received my entire comprehensive report from Early Warnings Services. A XXXX XXXX senior fraud representative from their corporate office called me asking why I insisted on having them look at the information on file that has nothing to do with XXXX XXXX. EWS considers itself a consumer reporting agency, and as such, must abide by the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) standards. EWS does not follow any prescribed rules issued as guidance and regulation from the FTC. 
Sending out bank data to financial institutions about all disputes published by EWS is an actionable offense. EWS can be subject to numerous fines because they did violate the very rules they claim to follow on their website. EWS is sending my entire report to banks/alternative lending & financial institutions that have nothing to do with a particular dispute, or the financial institution receives my dispute, along with disputes issued with other banks that have nothing to do with them. 

- Discontinue sending the disputed info disputed for one bank, to all banks listed on the report that is not required nor should have access to said data ( Employees have stated at EWS ; this action should not have taken place ). 

- I have sent numerous disputes to EWS and confirmed with employees that EWS created errors. Mistakes such as dual, triple, and reporting the same account four to five times, with a different variation of corresponding account number and routing number. There are numerous instances where I have one account with a particular bank, yet EWS reports five, even six versions of the same account.

- Early Warning Services will claim that they receive information reflected on the report from banks. However, after contacting the financial institutions that I conduct business with, they did not issue the information displayed on the EWS reports because the account and routing numbers don't exist in their system, nor are they associated with my name. As such, EWS needs to take accountability and remove the information that I have been disputing for years. 

- EWS reps, for years, have told me this would removals would occur and never took place, regardless of disputing info in writing via traditional mail, fax and email. 

- I am not the only individual to go through this. According to the complaint data via CFPB, under the topic " Improper use of your report '' and sub-issue " reporting company used your report improperly '' it is within the top ten most problematic issues consumers have with EWS. I will be sure to continue disputing this issue with Early Warning Services, via CFPB within this particular sub-topic until it becomes the most popular sub-issue within the topics available for selection. This action will not only create more awareness for consumers to understand how their data is being mishandled but also prove that EWS is modifying disputed information to remain on file with on the EWS database illicitly. 

- FTC/CFPB should punish EWS for providing the entirety of a consumer report to all banks listed on file with the customer on the EWS database, even if the customer does not have an account with them. 

- EWS refuses to dispute with a specific financial institution, thus exposing consumer data ripe for using indiscriminately. EWS does not read through the entirety of complaints and sends complaints in bulk to all banks. Posting the entire comprehensive report ( EWS most detailed form, my comprehensive was 77 pages ) to all banks listed on file, contrasts with traditional credit reporting agencies such as XXXX, and XXXX, where if you dispute information to a particular entity/financial institution, the single dispute for a specific issue is received by them, and not the entirety of the report. 

- I want to reiterate that my comprehensive report was over seventy pages long and over twenty-five financial institutions, including  banks, credit unions, alternative lending corporations all contacted me asking why they received disputes regarding banks they have nothing to do with the matter. On top of this, my data like social security number, birth date, even transactions, and checks were recorded by EWS to companies that have nothing to do with a particular dispute. Executive members at XXXX XXXX, which is part of the consortium of financial institutions that fund EWS, were very concerned that my data about other banks/financial institutions and current disputes were getting sent to them. There were concerns regarding data that sent to other commercial entities that have no business at looking at my info, listed on the EWS comprehensive consumer report because EWS sent this information. 

- For clarity, my situation has nothing to do with getting rejected for application to a bank. Specifically, this has to do with disputing info direct to EWS, and they are not being held accountable. This fact will change. Now that EWS is running Zelle, and more American Consumers become aware of the fraudulent practices Early Warning Carries out ; they will have no choice but to abide by the law. 

- For comparison, Early Warning Services is similar to a government-sponsored entity like a XXXX  XXXX, or XXXX XXXX. Unfortunately for Early Warning Services, the US Government does not sponsor them and does not wield an iota of power. They are beholden to the very sponsors that fund them ; the largest banks in The United States. Consistent instances of incompetence, fraud, and negligence will undergo investigation ; as complaints continue to mount against them, action will be taken to either dismantle the organization or remove every last incompetent employee ( all current employees at EWS ) they have proven useless at carrying out. EWS is abusing their " sponsorship '' via largest banks in the United States and attempting to leverage that influence over consumers by not following standards set forth by the fair credit reporting act. 

- EWS will abide by my requests sent via standard mail, fax, email, and now via CFPB.

consumer_complaint_narrative:
Starting XX/XX/XXXX, I asked American Express ( where my wife and I have credit cards ) to stop sending any financial information ( payment dates, amount paid, etc. ) of ALL of their cardholders to XXXX. XXXX has admitted allowing hackers to steal personal information from over XXXX,000,000 individuals. They can no longer be trusted with any of our personal information relating to credit card payments, mortgages, etc. Not only they gross negligent, but as Senate hearings in XX/XX/XXXX showed, XXXX  is now making millions more from its mistakes by pushing its monthly fee program to protect you from identity theft. XXXX is like the arsonist who burns down your house then says " For $ XXXX/month I 'll give you notice if I plan to do it again. '' I sent American express three emails explaining in detail why I did not want them to send any more financial information of all its cardholders to XXXX. If they simply stopped sending my and wife 's monthly information, our credit scores would plummet ( as XXXX warned me would happen when I spoke to them ). So only if American Express stops sending ALL its cardholders information, can this be accomplished. 

Not hearing back for eight weeks, I believed I was due the courtesy of a response since my emails were forwarded by a top American express executive to what she called their " credit risk leadership. '' The latter 's response, which I received on XX/XX/XXXX, said they were " continuously evaluating our relationship with XXXX to determine the best way to move forward. '' This is gobbledygook. Since the XXXX scandal broke, they have had months to evaluate their relationship. While they are " evaluating '' they have sent thousands of piece of financial information from their cardholders -- including us -- to XXXX which has shown its complete inability to protect it. What 's left to evaluate? 

What other reasons might American Express have to not discontinue sending its cardholders ' information to XXXX? One recent XXXX XXXX article pointed to the lending industry 's preference for using XXXX when checking out someone 's credit because XXXX combined the information from several of the other credit reporting companies. Apparently, according to this article, credit reports may be full of errors so that using XXXX ( rather than a single report from XXXX or XXXX ) is better because it minimizes the chance for errors ( in other words, if you combine a lot of XXXX, you 'll likely to get a horse, if you believe that! ). Assuming the above is correct, if American Express stops sending its cardholders ' information to XXXX, XXXX likely will have to go out of the credit report business. American Express will then have to order credit reports -- one nor more -- from XXXX, XXXX, or other smaller companies. This may cost American express more money that simply getting a combined report now from XXXX. This will cut into American Express 's profits. Is that why they are still evaluating '' their position? lastly, if XXXX is so important to American Express and other credit card companies, some other business entity will rush into the field to fill the gap and provide this service. the point is that it is criminal ina very broad sense for any credit card co. to send it 's cardholders ' information to XXXX EVER again. But they are still doing it until ordered to stop to protect the consumers and borrowers of this country. 

Below is an edited portion of what I wrote American Express on XX/XX/XXXX. They simply have avoided answering my specific concerns. They are stonewalling the issue : If I was sitting with your leadership credit reporting team, this is what Id ask them to consider : 1.  There is no way ever to trust XXXX again with the financial information you continue to send them. I dont care if they defensively say one person pushed a wrong button. They needed wall-after-wall of protection and it was their job to protect our information that you sent them. It will be laughable if you continue to send them information and say we can trust them now not to do that again. Sorry, one XXXX XXXX like thisXXXX million!!!! -- and youre out! 

2. If you cant refute the first premise, it follows you must stop sending them your cardholders financial information. 

3. Ive read some arguments that we need the big three credit reporting companies because there are so many mistakes in these reports that lenders who review a consumers credit pick and choose among the three to make sure applicants are creditworthy. My response is other than certain federal mortgage loans which require, I believe by regulation and not statute, all three reports, there is no magic in requiring three reports. Many companies, like yours I believe, use less. If there is a need for more than one report, the market will encourage the creation of a new or the expansion of an existing credit reporting company. Necessity will be the mother of invention ( without XXXX being part of it ).

4. Ive read some arguments that you should wait on taking action because all the lawsuits filed will address the problem by destroying XXXX credit reporting business. We all know how efficient the legal process is on such suits and we all will be six feet under when the verdicts come in. Its a copout to leave this to the courts when all you have to do is turn the spigot off and keep your information about your cardholders from XXXX. 

5. You might say XXXX, well stop sending your information to XXXX if you request so in writing. XXXX answered that. Except as otherwise provided in this section, a consumer reporting agency shall block the reporting of any information in the file of a consumer that the consumer identifies as information that resulted from an alleged identity theft, not later than 4 business days after the date of receipt by such agency of ( 1 ) appropriate proof of the identity of the consumer ; ( 2 ) a copy of an identity theft report ; ( 3 ) the identification of such information by the consumer ; and ( 4 ) a statement by the consumer that the information is not information relating to any transaction by the consumer. ( b ) Notification. A consumer reporting agency shall promptly notify the furnisher of information identified by the consumer under subsection ( a ) of this section ( 1 ) that the information may be a result of identity theft ; ( 2 ) that an identity theft report has been filed ; ( 3 ) that a block has been requested under this section ; and ( 4 ) of the effective dates of the block. ( c ) Authority to decline or rescind. ( 1 ) In general. A consumer reporting agency may decline to block, or may rescind any block, of information relating to a consumer under this section, if the consumer reporting agency reasonably determines that ( A ) the information was blocked in error or a block was requested by the consumer in error ; ( B ) the information was blocked, or a block was requested by the consumer, on the basis of a material misrepresentation of fact by the consumer relevant to the request to block ; or ( C ) the consumer obtained possession of goods, services, or money as a result of the blocked transaction or transactions. ( 2 ) Notification to consumer. If a block of information is declined or rescinded under this subsection, the affected consumer shall be notified promptly, in the same manner as consumers are notified of the reinsertion of information under section 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ) of this title. ( 3 ) Significance of block. For purposes of this subsection, if a consumer reporting agency rescinds a block, the presence of information in the file of a consumer prior to the blocking of such information is not evidence of whether the consumer knew or should have known that the consumer obtained possession of any goods, services, or money as a result of the block. ( d ) Exception for resellers. ( 1 ) No reseller file. This section shall not apply to a consumer reporting agency, if the consumer reporting agency ( A ) is a reseller ; ( B ) is not, at the time of the request of the consumer under subsection ( a ) of this section, otherwise furnishing or reselling a consumer report concerning the information identified by the consumer ; and ( C ) informs the consumer, by any means, that the consumer may report the identity theft to the Bureau to obtain consumer information regarding identity theft. ( 2 ) Reseller with file. The sole obligation of the consumer reporting agency under this section, with regard to any request of a consumer under this section, shall be to block the consumer report maintained by the consumer reporting agency from any subsequent use, if ( A ) the consumer, in accordance with the provisions of subsection ( a ) of this section, identifies, to a consumer reporting agency, information in the file of the consumer that resulted from identity theft ; and ( B ) the consumer reporting agency is a reseller of the identified information. ( 3 ) Notice. In carrying out its obligation under paragraph ( 2 ), the reseller shall promptly provide a notice to the consumer of the decision to block the file. Such notice shall contain the name, address, and telephone number of each consumer reporting agency from which the consumer information was obtained for resale. ( e ) Exception for verification companies. The provisions of this section do not apply to a check services company, acting as such, which issues authorizations for the purpose of approving or processing negotiable instruments, electronic fund transfers, or similar methods of payments, except that, beginning 4 business days after receipt of information described in paragraphs ( 1 ) through ( 3 ) of subsection ( a ) of this section, a check services company shall not report to a national consumer reporting agency described in section 1681a ( p ) of this title, any information identified in the subject identity theft report as resulting from identity theft. ( f ) Access to blocked information by law enforcement agencies. No provision of this section shall be construed as requiring a consumer reporting agency to prevent a Federal, State, or local law enforcement agency from accessing blocked information in a consumer file to which the agency could otherwise obtain access under this subchapter.

On XX/XX/2023, I purchased a program called XXXX XXXX XXXX  by XXXX XXXX for {$2400.00}. He promised that, through his program, we would make a guaranteed payout of $ XXXX {$6000.00} per month, without having to do anything, as it would all be managed by his team.

Additionally, after paying for a program that was advertised as " Done For You, '' it turned out to be a " Do It Yourself '' program instead. I had purchased the program because I have neither the time nor the financial expertise to run trades at this level. That is why I was counting on his promises of having his " team '' run the trades for me, using their A.I. bots. However, XXXX switched everything up. I tried reaching out to his customer support for a refund, and they just ignored me. I then reached out to my bank ( Credit Karma, through XXXX XXXX  ) to file a dispute, as I have plenty of evidence to prove that this was a scam. ( See attachment - My XXXX Dispute ) On XX/XX/2023, after trying unsuccessfully to secure a refund from XXXX 's customer support team, I filed a dispute ( # XXXX ) with Credit Karma/XXXXXXXXXXXX XXXX to have them investigate the issue. On their dispute form, they had no way for me to even submit or upload any evidence, so I wrote out my complaint instead, and also let them know that I do have evidence to submit if they need to see it. No one from Credit Karma ever contacted me throughout their entire investigation to see my evidence. How are they able to fairly investigate a dispute without the full facts and without seeing evidence from me? What are they even investigating with NO evidence? 

On XX/XX/2023, I was given a {$2400.00} provisional credit with a letter, stating that they are required to provisionally credit my account for the amount in question within 10 business days of acknowledging the dispute. They said that the final resolution would be no more than 90 calendar days from the date of the claim. ( Their letter is included as an attachment here. See attachment - Provisional Credit Notification ). 

In the meantime, I spoke with several other people who had also purchased this program, and they had submitted evidence of the scam to their banks or XXXX ( whichever they had used ), and ALL of them had received refunds from XXXX or their banks and within a MUCH faster time frame than 90 days. ( I have included an attachment that shows 5 different people in a group Im a part of, who all received refunds from their financial institutions for their disputes against XXXX XXXX. See attachment - Received Refunds ) During the course of this investigation, I reached out to Credit Karma MULTIPLE times, both through phone and email, about why I had still not been allowed to submit evidence. They simply told me, In case that is necessary, the specialized department is going to be contacting you to request the information. ( I have also included the email here where they said this. See attachment - Credit Karma Email XXXX ). But once again, NO ONE ever contacted me. Every time I reached out to Credit Karma about this, I was told that the dispute team would reach out to me, but no one ever did. 

Then, on XX/XX/2023, the {$2400.00} provisional credit was snatched back out of my account, with a note saying that my dispute was unsuccessful. There was not even a letter sent to me with any kind of explanation simply a note attached to the dispute that said Unsuccessful. ( See attachment - Dispute Unsuccessful ) I have asked several times to see an explanation of the findings or results of their investigation and why they found in favor of XXXX XXXX over me. I am owed an explanation. After snatching {$2400.00} out of my account, they did not even have the decency to provide me with any explanation of why they had come to this decision. It was bad enough that I was scammed, but now they have added salt to the wound by siding with the scammer, without even bothering to let me know WHY. 

After this, I reached out to Credit Karma several times through email, chat, and phone, and they still refuse to tell me why they have reached this decision. They did not even give me an opportunity to appeal the decision, which I thought was required after a bank reaches a decision in a dispute. 

On XX/XX/2023, I spoke to a Credit Karma chat representative named XXXX, who was very rude. I told her that I wanted to know the explanation and details of the investigation, as well as why I was not provided with an opportunity to appeal the decision. Instead, she decided that she no longer wanted to chat with me about it and ended the chat. ( See chat attachment - Credit Karma Chat XXXX ) Later the same day ( XX/XX/2023 ), I spoke with Credit Karma support through email. I explained the same situation to them and was told that they would escalate my case to a team of specialists who are more equipped to help me. ( See attachment - Credit Karma Email XXXX ) They then told me that I could attach any evidence to the email. I responded and attached a document, which included evidence. Once again, no one ever got back with me about this. 

I reached out AGAIN on XX/XX/2023 and AGAIN included my document with all of my evidence. They said AGAIN that it seems like this case would be better handled by our specialized team, so they promised they would escalate it and that I would receive the assistance that I need. ( See attachment - Credit Karma Email XXXX ). However, unsurprisingly by now, no one ever contacted me after that. 

By now, I am fed up. Every single time I reach out to their support team, I am told that my issue will be escalated to a specialized team, yet I never, ever hear back after they say that. No one from any specialized team or dispute team ever gets back to me, and there is no way for me to contact this so-called team. It seems to me that this is just a way to pacify me. They have still not explained what led them to reach their decision in my dispute and why they allowed XXXX XXXX to keep my {$2400.00}. They have also not allowed me to appeal this decision. 

It does not appear that anyone has bothered to even review my evidence. This is an EXTREMELY unprofessional way to operate a bank. They have dropped the ball numerous times in this case. This is nearly {$2500.00}. I dont have that kind of money to waste. It seems to me like they could care less, and they didnt even bother to review any evidence from me without deciding in the merchants favor. That is not fair to me, as a client. At the very least, I deserve a fair judgment in this dispute. You can not judge a dispute fairly without reviewing the evidence. They continue to ignore me and pacify me, because its not important to them. But its important to ME. This is MY money, and they have supported a scammer getting away with it.

consumer_complaint_narrative: ( a ) Block. Except as otherwise provided in this section, a consumer reporting agency shall block the reporting of any information in the file of a consumer that the consumer identifies as information that resulted from an alleged identity theft, not later than 4 business days after the date of receipt by such agency of ( 1 ) appropriate proof of the identity of the consumer ; ( 2 ) a copy of an identity theft report ; ( 3 ) the identification of such information by the consumer; and ( 4 ) a statement by the consumer that the information is not information relating to any transaction by the consumer. ( b ) Notification. A consumer reporting agency shall promptly notify the furnisher of information identified by the consumer under subsection ( a ) of this section ( 1 ) that the information may be a result of identity theft ; ( 2 ) that an identity theft report has been filed ; ( 3 ) that a block has been requested under this section; and ( 4 ) of the effective dates of the block. ( c ) Authority to decline or rescind. ( 1 ) In general. A consumer reporting agency may decline to block, or may rescind any block, of information relating to a consumer under this section, if the consumer reporting agency reasonably determines that ( A ) the information was blocked in error or a block was requested by the consumer in error ; ( B ) the information was blocked, or a block was requested by the consumer, on the basis of a material misrepresentation of fact by the consumer relevant to the request to block ; or ( C ) the consumer obtained possession of goods, services, or money as a result of the blocked transaction or transactions. ( 2 ) Notification to consumer. If a block of information is declined or rescinded under this subsection, the affected consumer shall be notified promptly, in the same manner as consumers are notified of the reinsertion of information under section 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( B ) of this title. ( 3 ) Significance of block. For purposes of this subsection, if a consumer reporting agency rescinds a block, the presence of information in the file of a consumer prior to the blocking of such information is not evidence of whether the consumer knew or should have known that the consumer obtained possession of any goods, services, or money as a result of the block. ( d ) Exception for resellers. ( 1 ) No reseller file. This section shall not apply to a consumer reporting agency, if the consumer reporting agency ( A ) is a reseller ; ( B ) is not, at the time of the request of the consumer under subsection ( a ) of this section, otherwise furnishing or reselling a consumer report concerning the information identified by the consumer ; and ( C ) informs the consumer, by any means, that the consumer may report the identity theft to the Bureau to obtain consumer information regarding identity theft. ( 2 ) Reseller with file. The sole obligation of the consumer reporting agency under this section, with regard to any request of a consumer under this section, shall be to block the consumer report maintained by the consumer reporting agency from any subsequent use, if ( A ) the consumer, in accordance with the provisions of subsection ( a ) of this section, identifies, to a consumer reporting agency, information in the file of the consumer that resulted from identity theft ; and ( B ) the consumer reporting agency is a reseller of the identified information. ( 3 ) Notice. In carrying out its obligation under paragraph ( 2 ), the reseller shall promptly provide a notice to the consumer of the decision to block the file. Such notice shall contain the name, address, and telephone number of each consumer reporting agency from which the consumer information was obtained for resale. ( e ) Exception for verification companies. The provisions of this section do not apply to a check services company, acting as such, which issues authorizations for the purpose of approving or processing negotiable instruments, electronic fund transfers, or similar methods of payments, except that, beginning 4 business days after receipt of information described in paragraphs ( 1 ) through ( 3 ) of subsection ( a ) of this section, a check services company shall not report to a national consumer reporting agency described in section 1681a ( p ) of this title, any information identified in the subject identity theft report as resulting from identity theft. ( f ) Access to blocked information by law enforcement agencies. No provision of this section shall be construed as requiring a consumer reporting agency to prevent a Federal, State, or local law enforcement agency from accessing blocked information in a consumer file to which the agency could otherwise obtain access under this subchapter

I was told my name, ss #, dob and an email address. Which is XXXX to say the least. They have no idea who's on the other end of the computer.
